rv.q: It is playful but powerful, with a stripped-back aesthetic that declutters the classic text of layers of excess Victoriana but retains a sure sense of time and place.

He can, of course, pull off Ebenezer’s dourness, but as in Doctor Who, he’s brilliant at exuding an unguarded, childlike joy, as Scrooge realises it’s not too late to change his ways.Continues... A new and returning cast provides excellent support. Frances McNamee is great as Belle, Scrooge’s lost love.
With complimentary satsumas and mince pies, hand bells and two flurries of menthol-scented snow foam, any sense of resistance is futile.
I struggle to think of another show that captures the Christmas spirit as perfectly as this one does.
